rawCommits.subject: fix(ci): add missing Z_BILLING_API_KEY to stable release build
rawCommits.body:
The secret was passed in release-nightly.yml but missing from
release-stable.yml, so stable desktop builds compiled with an empty
billing API key. This caused grant_signup_credits to silently skip
on every desktop login — no welcome credits, no daily credits, no
pro top-up.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: add missing Z_BILLING_API_KEY to stable release build

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): plumb new-session flag through image / 3D / video modes
rawCommits.body:
Clicking the chat-input "+" affordance set `nextSendStartsNewSession` on
the per-partition send control, but only the regular chat fall-through
path forwarded it to the server. Image / 3D / video sends routed through
`generate*Stream` (and the matching server handlers' `resolve_persist_ctx`
which always called `setup_*_chat_persistence` with `force_new=false /
pinned_session_id=None`) silently appended to the latest existing
session, so picking a non-code mode and pressing "+" never actually
started a new conversation.

Frontend: extend `generateImageStream`, `generate3dStream`,
`generateVideoStream` with optional `newSession` / `sessionId` and
forward `shouldStartNewSession` + `sessionIdRef.current` from both
`useChatStream` and `useAgentChatStream` (also fixes
`useStandaloneAgentChat`).

Backend: add `new_session` / `session_id` to `GenerateImageRequest`,
`Generate3dRequest`, and `GenerateVideoRequest`, then thread them
through `resolve_persist_ctx` into the existing
`setup_*_chat_persistence` plumbing. Downstream `pick_candidate_session`
already prioritises `force_new=true` over a pin (covered by
`resolve_force_new_overrides_pin` in `agents/chat/persist.rs`), so a
stale `?session=` in the URL no longer wins over an explicit "+" press.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: plumb new-session flag through image / 3D / video modes

rawCommits.subject: fix(updater): eliminate ping subprocess so Windows update no longer flashes a terminal
rawCommits.body:
The previous fix (22694c181) dropped DETACHED_PROCESS so CREATE_NO_WINDOW
would be honored, on the theory that cmd.exe would then own a hidden
console which child console apps (ping.exe) would inherit silently. In
practice, once the parent aura.exe has exited that inheritance is not
reliable -- Windows can still allocate a freshly-visible console for
the child for a split second, which is exactly the flash users keep
seeing.

The settle delay isn't load-bearing either: by the time the script
runs ping, the NSIS installer has already exited (we just captured its
ERRORLEVEL), so its file handles are released by Windows, and the
subsequent `start "" "!AURA_EXE!"` targets the installed exe, not the
installer.

Drop the `ping -n 2 127.0.0.1 > nul` settle delay from the handoff
.bat, update the surrounding rationale comments to reflect the new
invariant (no console subprocesses in the script, period), and add
`handoff_script_has_no_console_subprocesses` to pin it as a regression
test. CREATE_NO_WINDOW and the breakaway-from-job retry are kept as
defense-in-depth.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: eliminate ping subprocess so Windows update no longer flashes a terminal

The end-of-turn error row was forcing the full diagnostic onto a single

title tooltip. Stack the chrome instead: line 1 carries the wrapping error

rawCommits.subject: feat(chat): wire plan mode to a shared spec-planning policy that blocks code edits
rawCommits.body:
Plan mode (`action=generate_specs` / public `mode=plan`) now routes
through `handlers::plan_mode` so the spec-planning prompt, the
read-only tool surface, and the hard-disabled code-writing tools stay
identical across the auth'd chat handlers (instance + agent routes),
the public-chat handler, and the dedicated `/specs/generate*`
endpoints. Cold-start sessions stamp the policy onto `SessionConfig`
(suffixed system prompt + `tool_permissions` off entries for
write/edit/delete/run/git/dev-loop tools); warm sessions still see a
per-turn preamble wrapper + plan-mode `tool_hints` so a session that
opened in code mode still gets steered into plan-mode behaviour on a
plan turn, and flipping back to code mode produces an unwrapped turn
so the model does not carry plan-mode framing forward.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: wire plan mode to a shared spec-planning policy that blocks code edits

rawCommits.subject: chat-input: keep textarea focused when switching models
rawCommits.body:
Switching models used to blur the chat textarea because (a) the
ModelPicker trigger button grabbed focus on mousedown by default
and (b) ChatInputBar explicitly called shellRef.current?.blur() in
its onOpen handler. Mirror the SlidingPills pattern: preventDefault
the mousedown on the trigger and the menu wrapper so opening the
picker and selecting a model both leave the caret exactly where the
user left it. Add a ModelPicker regression test covering both paths.

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): drop new-session pin when user selects a session before sending
rawCommits.body:
The "+" affordance in the chat input bar arms `nextSendStartsNewSession`
so the next send forces a fresh harness session id. The pin lived in
the per-partition `partition-send-control` map (project route) and a
hook-scoped ref (standalone / chat-app), so it survived navigation.
If the user pressed "+", then clicked an existing session row before
typing, the next send still POSTed `new_session=true` and the server
minted a brand-new session id. `SessionReady` then flipped the URL
away from the clicked row, so the message visibly landed in a new
chat instead of extending the one the user selected.

Clear the pin in both hooks when `sessionId` transitions to a real
value -- the user has made an explicit "extend THIS session" choice.
Also reset the standalone ref when `core.key` changes, since (unlike
the project map) it isn't partition-keyed and would otherwise leak a
"+" press from agent A into the first send on agent B inside the
chat-app shell.

Tests cover the +/click/send sequence on the project route (plus the
image-mode variant) and both the session-pick and agent-swap cases on
the standalone hook.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: drop new-session pin when user selects a session before sending

rawCommits.body:

of a plain click toggle (with Enter/Space/Escape keyboard support),

rawCommits.subject: fix: harness session open hang + false stuck-stream pill on warm reopens
rawCommits.body:
Five layered changes fix the "Local timeout reached" / "Agent paused
for Ns ago" symptoms that fired on warm-reopened chat sessions:

* Frontend (interface/src/hooks/stream/store.ts): setIsStreaming now
  rebases lastEventAt and clears stuckSince on the false->true edge.
  Previously the watchdog inherited the prior turn's last-event
  timestamp, so a send after >30s of idle rendered the false-positive
  "Agent paused" pill at T=0 before any wire event could land. Locked
  in with three regression tests in store.test.ts and one
  integration-shaped case in use-stream-health.test.ts pinning the
  user-reported scenario.

* Frontend heartbeat handling (build-stream-handler.ts,
  use-agent-chat-stream.ts): silently consume the new
  progress:heartbeat frames the server emits during long awaits,
  keeping the stream-progress clock fresh without polluting the UI
  with a heartbeat indicator.

* Server safety net (apps/aura-os-server/src/handlers/agents/chat/
  streaming.rs): wrap SessionBridge::open_and_send_user_message in a
  60s tokio::time::timeout with begin/complete/TIMEOUT tracing.
  Backstop against any future class of harness hang we haven't yet
  observed; surfaces as a clean bad_gateway with a user-friendly
  "please retry or restart the harness" message.

* Harness client unblock (crates/aura-os-harness/src/local_harness.rs):
  subscribe to the bridge events_tx BEFORE sending SessionInit (so an
  immediate Error message isn't lost in the microseconds-wide race),
  and wrap the SessionReady recv loop in tokio::time::timeout(30s).
  The previous shape would hang forever when the harness WebSocket
  closed early, because the function itself owned events_tx so
  rx.recv() never saw Err(Closed). The 30s ceiling sits comfortably
  under the server's 60s outer timeout so the more informative
  message surfaces first.

* Companion harness-runtime changes ship in the aura-harness repo:
  classify_ws_frame now splits None/Err/Close into distinct
  CloseReason variants with structured ws_transport_error frames sent
  back over the wire, and the Wave 5 / T1.3 WS_MAX_FRAME_BYTES /
  WS_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES caps (64 KiB / 256 KiB) are removed in favour
  of tungstenite's 16 MiB / 64 MiB defaults. Those caps were
  artificially low for the Bearer-authed endpoints we run and were
  false-positiving on legitimate ~77 KiB SessionInit payloads.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: harness session open hang + false stuck-stream pill on warm reopens

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): keep queued prompts after turn ends + add Send-now affordance
rawCommits.body:
Queued prompts were disappearing instead of being replayed because
setIsStreaming(false) fires from inside SSE event handlers
(AssistantMessageEnd non-tool_use, Done, GenerationCompleted, errors)
while the outer async sendMessage / performSend is still awaiting the
stream close. The dequeue-on-completion effect in useChatPanelState
raced past the finally block, re-entered the hook, and was silently
swallowed by the in-flight latch.

Clear inFlightRef / ctrl.inFlight in lockstep with every
setIsStreaming(false) so the dequeue's re-entry now lands cleanly.
build-stream-handler gains an onStreamFinalized callback wired from
performSend to the same end so the project-chat hook follows the same
shape.

Also add a per-item "Send now" (lightning bolt) button in the queued
messages list. It's only visible while a stream is in flight; the
handler removes the item, calls onStop, then dispatches the queued
payload on the next microtask so the upstream stopStreaming finally
has time to settle.

Tests cover the latch-sync regression and the new force-send handler.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: keep queued prompts after turn ends + add Send-now affordance

Both signals are derived from `selectAgentActivity` so the indicator

rawCommits.subject: agents: also light avatar ring during chat (not just automation loops)
rawCommits.body:
The previous pass only watched `loop-activity-store`, which is fed by
`LoopOpened` events that today are only emitted for `LoopKind::Automation`
and `Spec`. Regular chat turns never open a registry loop, so an
agent mid-response in the agents-app sidebar showed nothing.

Add `useIsAgentBusy(agentId)` that aggregates the three independent
"this template is working" signals into a single boolean:

  - automation loop activity for the template (existing path)
  - standalone-agent chat stream (`useAgentChatStream` keys its
    stream-store entry by template `agentId` directly)
  - project-agent chat stream (`useChatStream` stamps the
    project-scoped `agentInstanceId` into the sidekick store; we
    map every known instance of this template back via
    `projects-list-store.agentsByProject`)

Wire `AgentConversationRow` through the new hook so the avatar
ring and pulsing status dot light up the moment the user sends a
chat to any binding of the template, not just when an automation
loop is running.

rawCommits.subject: agents: rotate the busy ring reliably + drop reduce-motion gate
rawCommits.body:
The ring rendered but stayed frozen on Windows: rotating the inner
`<svg>` via CSS is unreliable (some browsers ignore
`transform-origin: center` on SVG roots and rotate around the SVG
coordinate origin instead), and any user with OS-level "reduce
motion" enabled hit the `@media` guard and saw a static dashed
outline that read as decoration rather than activity.

Move the animation onto the wrapping `<span>` (plain HTML box —
`transform-origin: 50% 50%` is well-defined and consistent across
browsers), and drop the `prefers-reduced-motion` guard so behavior
matches the sibling `LoopProgress` spinner which also always spins.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): make queue Send-now actually cancel + dispatch + render
rawCommits.body:
Three stacked races caused the force-send affordance to silently drop
the queued prompt and leave the UI looking like nothing happened:

1. `stopStreaming` (both `useAgentChatStream` and `useChatStream`)
   aborted the controller but only cleared `inFlightRef` / `ctrl.inFlight`
   from the outer async fn's `finally` — which fires in a microtask
   after the SSE close propagates. The Send-now handler dispatched the
   chosen prompt right after calling stop, so `sendMessage` saw a
   stale `inFlight === true` and returned silently. Clear the latch
   synchronously in `stopStreaming` so the very next dispatch lands.

2. The aborted turn's `finally` then ran and unconditionally reset
   the latch even though a fresh send had already taken over the
   partition, clobbering the new turn's sync re-entry guard. Move
   the latch reset inside the existing "still my turn"
   (`abortRef.current === controller` / `ctrl.currentController ===
   controller`) block so old tails can't stomp on a new send.

3. Browsers don't synchronously flush an SSE reader's internal queue
   on `abort()`. Buffered frames from the aborted turn still drove
   the stale handler closure, calling `setIsStreaming(false)` and
   resetting the stream buffer on the new turn. Guard the handler's
   `onEvent`/`onError`/`onDone` with `controller.signal.aborted` so
   the new turn owns the partition uncontested.

With the latch now clear synchronously, `handleQueueSendNow` can
dispatch inline; React 18 batches the `setIsStreaming(false → true)`
toggles so the dequeue-on-completion effect never sees a `true → false`
blip to race against.

Regression coverage:
- `use-agent-chat-stream.test.ts`: calls `stopStreaming()` and
  `sendMessage()` in the same synchronous tick and asserts both
  messages reach the wire even before the first turn's `finally`
  runs — the exact pattern Send-now produces.
- `useChatPanelState.test.tsx`: asserts inline `onStop → onSend`
  dispatch order instead of the prior microtask-deferred path.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: make queue Send-now actually cancel + dispatch + render

Add hasDesktopBridge check alongside isNativeApp so desktop falls

rendered.title: Plan mode, prompt caching, and a deep pass on chat session reliability
rendered.intro: Today's nightly is dominated by chat-surface work: a unified plan mode that hard-blocks code edits, end-to-end prompt-cache accounting from the harness to the context popover, and a long sequence of fixes that make new-session pins, queued prompts, and warm session reopens behave the way users expect. The Windows updater stops flashing a terminal, and a missing CI secret that had been silently breaking signup credits on stable desktop builds is restored.

entries.title: Stable desktop signup credits restored
entries.summary: A missing CI secret was silently breaking welcome, daily, and pro top-up credits on stable desktop builds.

items.text: Added the missing Z_BILLING_API_KEY to the stable release workflow so grant_signup_credits no longer no-ops on desktop login — welcome credits, daily credits, and pro top-up now flow on stable builds.

entries.title: New-session button now works in image, 3D, and video modes
entries.summary: The chat input's '+' affordance was silently appending to the latest session whenever a non-code mode was active.

items.text: Image, 3D, and video generation requests now thread the new_session and session_id flags from the frontend stream helpers all the way through resolve_persist_ctx, so pressing '+' in any mode genuinely starts a fresh conversation instead of being overridden by a stale ?session= in the URL.

entries.title: Windows updater stops flashing a console window
entries.summary: The handoff script no longer spawns a console subprocess after the installer exits.

items.text: Removed the ping-based settle delay from the Windows updater handoff .bat so child consoles can no longer briefly flash during update install; CREATE_NO_WINDOW and the breakaway-from-job retry remain as defense-in-depth, and a regression test pins that the handoff script contains no console subprocesses.

entries.title: Readable, copyable error chrome on chat messages
entries.summary: End-of-turn error details are no longer hidden behind an ellipsised single line.

items.text: Chat error rows now stack over two lines: the full wrapping error message with a one-click copy button on line 1, and the Support ID chip, Report bug action, and variant-specific actions like Buy credits on line 2 — so contract-blocked diagnostics are finally readable in place.

entries.title: Plan mode unified behind a strict spec-planning policy
entries.summary: Plan mode now uses a shared policy that hard-disables code-writing tools across every chat surface.

items.text: Plan mode (action=generate_specs / public mode=plan) now routes through a single handlers::plan_mode module across the auth'd instance and agent routes, the public chat handler, and the /specs/generate* endpoints, applying the same spec-planning system prompt and read-only tool surface everywhere.

Cold-start sessions stamp the policy onto SessionConfig with tool_permissions off for write/edit/delete/run/git/dev-loop tools, while warm sessions get a per-turn preamble and plan-mode tool_hints — so flipping a code-mode session into plan mode is safe, and flipping back produces a clean unwrapped turn.

entries.title: Prompt-cache accounting, busy-state polish, and a fleet of chat session fixes
entries.summary: A long afternoon thread shipped end-to-end prompt-cache visibility, fixed several chat session races, added live agent activity indicators, and resolved the warm-reopen 'Agent paused' false positive.

items.text: Prompt-cache tokens are now tracked end-to-end: ContextBreakdown carries cache_read_tokens and cache_creation_tokens (with a demo-path backfill), session and dev-loop usage rollups accumulate cache_creation_input_tokens and cache_read_input_tokens toward context-window utilization, and the context-usage popover renders a new 'Cached this turn' row with hit percentage when data is present.

Each chat surface now derives a stable prompt_cache_key (agent, instance, tool, devloop) plumbed into SessionModelOverrides, and the direct-HTTP Anthropic calls for Haiku session titles, summaries, and the changelog generator attach cache_control: ephemeral plus the prompt-caching beta header so cache reads actually take effect on repeat calls.

Fixed the false 'Agent paused' / 'Local timeout reached' pill on warm-reopened sessions: the frontend stuck-stream watchdog now rebases lastEventAt on the streaming edge, the server emits a 15s progress:heartbeat SSE frame during quiet stretches, and SessionBridge::open_and_send_user_message is wrapped in a 60s server timeout with a 30s harness-side ceiling so hung opens surface a clean retry message instead of hanging forever.

Queued prompts no longer vanish when a turn ends, and a new per-item Send-now affordance (ArrowUp icon) lets users force a queued prompt past the in-flight turn. Three stacked races in stopStreaming — stale in-flight latches, finally-block clobbering, and buffered SSE frames after abort — were fixed so cancel + dispatch + render all land cleanly.

Pressing '+' and then clicking an existing session row before typing now correctly extends that session instead of minting a new one — the new-session pin is cleared when sessionId becomes a real value, and the standalone ref is reset on agent swap to prevent the pin leaking across agents in the chat-app shell.

Agents-app sidebar rows now light up an avatar ring and pulse the status dot whenever any binding of an agent template is working — automation loops, standalone-agent chats, or project-bound chats — via a new useIsAgentBusy hook. The ring's rotation was moved off the SVG onto the wrapping span for cross-browser reliability and slimmed to a subtler 1.4 stroke.

Chat input polish: switching models keeps the textarea focused, the context-usage popover now opens on click with keyboard support instead of hover (so stray pointer moves toward the composer stop covering it), and text selection inside the accent user bubble is finally visible by inverting the bubble's accent/contrast pair.

Block headers now render as div role=button with Enter/Space handling so trailing slots (like SpecBlock's CopyButton) no longer produce nested-button hydration warnings, and the noisy [attach] debug logs were removed from the chat-input attachment paths while keeping real FileReader warnings.

Desktop now correctly shows the login screen for logged-out users instead of the web-only public chat shell, by checking hasDesktopBridge alongside isNativeApp before falling through to LoggedOutShell.

highlights: Plan mode now hard-blocks code edits across every chat surface
Prompt-cache tokens are tracked end-to-end and shown in the context popover
Multiple chat session race conditions and queue bugs resolved
Windows updater no longer flashes a console window
Stable desktop signup credits restored via missing CI secret
